A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MetaTuner, with matching core methods and experiments. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results on MATH, GSM8K, HotpotQA, and CosmosQA, together with ablations, generalization experiments, and inference measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds chess and cross-model evaluations, soft co-optimization comparisons, expert-data sensitivity experiments, and efficiency results.

M1.justification: Appendix C.4 introduces MetaTuner-C, which clusters test queries and reuses a centroid's prompt and LoRA parameters across its cluster. This is a limited inference extension; the main MetaTuner-I/J architecture, generation components, and training objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The original four benchmarks remain, while Table 3 adds Checkmate in One Move, extending evaluation to chess. Figure 10 also expands distribution-shift coverage with held-out HotpotQA and CosmosQA evaluations beyond the earlier generalization experiment. These additions broaden task and test-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: v2 removes the standalone GPT-4o comparator from Table 1 and adds an evaluated prefix-tuning-plus-LoRA soft co-optimization baseline in Section 4.7/Figure 9. New cost comparisons include PPO, DPO, BPO, and RLPrompt. The other main benchmark comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and hyperparameter searches remain. New protocols include Llama3.1-8B, Llama3.2-3B, and Mistral-7B configurations; training-cost comparisons on two 80GB GPUs including data collection; clustering sweeps at K=10, 30, and 50; and warm-up experiments using 20%/60% expert data or Qwen2.5-14B/32B experts.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis through additional OOD experiments, comparisons of learned prompts across models and tasks, training/inference cost breakdowns, clustering accuracy-latency tradeoffs, and sensitivity to expert-data quantity and quality. The original component ablations, rollout/sharing analyses, and MATH case study are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates; approximate runtimes do not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Shared Table 1 entries, Table 2 ablations, and warm-up scores are unchanged, but GPT-4o results are removed and substantial new results are added. For example, Table 9 reports 40.00 accuracy at 0.46 seconds for 3B MetaTuner-C with K=50 versus 41.33 at 0.73 seconds for MetaTuner-J. Incremental LoRA costs in Tables 7–8 also reverse v1 Table 3's backbone assignments, without explaining a measurement change.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds the amortized generation-cost expression t=K(tp+tq)/N and identifies MetaTuner-J as the K=N case. Equations 1–9 remain unchanged. The added multitask-generalization discussion is qualitative and citation-based, without a new formal bound or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: joint prompt/parameter optimization, shared representations, supervised regularization, and improved effectiveness and robustness. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations linking generalization to multitask representation sharing, discrete prompts to reduced representation collapse and overfitting, and prompt specificity to model capacity. It also interprets reduced expert dependence and discusses training/latency tradeoffs. The existing limitations in Appendix B remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reported project/code-release link, additional model checkpoint names, and training-cost details. Conversely, explicit GPT-4o and NVIDIA A100 identifiers become generic proprietary-LLM and 80GB-GPU descriptions, and the specified single-GPU inference setup disappears. These disclosure changes do not establish actual substitutions of models or hardware.

R1.justification: v2 adds references connecting the work to soft-prompt representation collapse and multitask generalization, including Bhardwaj, Razdaibiedina, Baxter, and Maurer, while removing the GPT-4o system-card reference. The main related-work taxonomy and positioning against BetterTogether remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. Changes include local wording edits, an additional research question and Section 4.7, expanded appendix subsections, author/affiliation updates, acknowledgements, and author-year citations. The existing argument is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR title/header layout, adjusts Figure 1 typography and legends, and adds substantial graphical and tabular material for comparisons, generalization, prompt examples, costs, and sensitivity tests. The old MATH case becomes Figure 11, while the original parameter-generation cost table is replaced by fuller backbone-specific breakdowns.

improvement.justification: The soft co-optimization control, expert-data sensitivity tests, and fuller cost accounting address concrete gaps in v1's validation and practical assessment. These benefits are tempered by reduced specificity about expert models/hardware and reporting inconsistencies. In particular, v2 Table 3 reports MetaTuner-J at 18.44 versus BetterTogether at 34.44 on Llama3.2-3B/MATH despite claiming consistent wins. The added evidence provides a limited net improvement rather than an unequivocal substantial gain.
